basis: Inherited impairment of erythroid, megakaryocytic and sometimes neutrophil development causes cytopenias and bleeding.
Blocked, fluid-distended fallopian tube; reproductive organs have no axis. Infection is not intrinsic to the diagnosis.
Distal limb and renal malformations define the syndrome; ocular and palatal abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Spontaneous transmural esophageal rupture defines the disease; secondary infection and pleural complications are not intrinsic defining lesions.
Tumor occupies the spinal epidural compartment surrounding the cord; vertebral bone invasion is not required by the definition.
Congenital obstruction within the right ventricular outflow tract; pulmonary refers to cardiac outflow, not lung disease.
Palmar and plantar skin injury defines the syndrome. Tingling alone does not establish peripheral nerve damage.
Inherited myxomatous mitral valve prolapse with regurgitation is a structural cardiac valve disorder.
Severe alpha-thalassemia; heart failure occurs in 80-99% and hydrocephalus in 30-79%. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic dysfunction.
Progressive skeletal muscle degeneration defines the myopathy; distal sensory impairment in 30-79% supports additional peripheral neurologic dysfunction.
NEUROD1-related monogenic diabetes; neurologic abnormalities are not established as common in heterozygous MODY6.
Y-chromosome rearrangement primarily affecting sex development and fertility; common endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ damage is not established.
Acute infectious inflammation of the fallopian tube; the reproductive site has no organ axis, but the infectious mechanism applies.
Benign tumor arising in breast or rarely prostate; both sites are outside the organ axes.
CRBN-related intellectual disability and developmental impairment define the disorder; seizures also affect the same axis.
Ectrodactyly, ectodermal dysplasia and oral clefting define EEC1. Common damaging ocular, renal or hearing involvement is not established for this subtype.
Multiple cutaneous nodules and urinary tract abnormalities define the syndrome; annotations include hydronephrosis and duplicated collecting systems.
Hereditary cancer syndrome defined by diffuse gastric cancer susceptibility; breast has no axis. No additional organ damage is inferred from risk.
Malignancy of B lymphocytes; lymphoma requires the immune mechanism axis. No specific extranodal organ is affected across most subtypes.
Congenital fusion and malformation of fingers, phalanges and toes define this isolated limb disorder.
Malignant neoplasm originating in the appendix; lymphoma is only a subtype, so its mechanism does not apply to the umbrella.
Developmental abnormality of maxillary alveolar bone, gingiva and teeth; both skeletal and oral structures are defining sites.
Apocrine metaplasia within breast adenosis; breast disease has no axis.
Autoinflammatory dermatitis and arthritis define YAOS; keratoconjunctivitis sicca affects 9/22 (~41%). GI symptoms alone do not establish tissue damage.
Ocular anomalies, shortened bones and ectodermal defects define the syndrome; congenital anodontia is a major defining feature in the reported sibship.
